3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: I walked down the palm-tree-lined path that connected Palas Rezna to the nearby House of Delegates.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: In contrast to the ornate palace, the House was essentially a plain concrete box. Its stripped-down appearance reflected its hurried construction.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: The only adornment was a phrase chiseled above the entrance: "Ax Populat Rizati."

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: I made my way down the hall to the meeting room.

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: Hugo rose to greet me as I entered the empty chamber. We took our seats atop the raised wooden platform in the center of the room.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: Directly below the platform were two podiums, one for each speaker. Wooden benches for the delegates were arranged in a circle around us.

13.speaker: Narrator
13.text: The clock struck ten and the delegates filed in.

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: Each wore a satin sash in the traditional color of his or her province: red for Rizia Imperii, blue for Valenqiris, yellow for Cardesse-Montaklar and green for Brenas.

15.speaker: Narrator
15.text: Next came the speakers. House Leader Daria de Rava walked out in a well-tailored crimson suit.

17.speaker: Player_Romus
17.text: "Which house does she belong to again?"

19.speaker: Hugo Toras
19.text: "The de Ravas aren't related to any of the royal houses. They were granted their nobility status through service to our family after the War of Succession."

20.speaker: Player_Romus
20.text: "Remind me, how did she land this job?"

21.speaker: Hugo Toras
21.text: "Technically, she's a Baroness. But she prefers the title of Madam Speaker."

22.speaker: Hugo Toras
22.text: "She performed superbly as the head of the provincial council in Rizia Imperii."

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: I noted the approving tone in his voice as he spoke of her.

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: Next came Manus Sazon, clad in a black suit with a forest-green silk tie. He waved to his fellow delegates, then to me.

27.speaker: Narrator
27.text: Daria picked up a golden bell and rang it once.

28.speaker: Daria de Rava
28.text: "Ladies and gentlemen, it is my privilege to call this meeting of the House of Delegates to order."

29.speaker: Daria de Rava
29.text: "Today we are humbled by the presence of His Majesty King Romus, long may he reign."

30.speaker: Narrator
30.text: A few cries of "Long may he reign!" echoed among the delegates, particularly those in red and blue sashes.

31.speaker: Daria de Rava
31.text: "The Rizian People's Party has prepared a proposal that Mr. Sazon will submit before the Delegates and His Majesty."

32.speaker: Daria de Rava
32.text: "Mr. Sazon, would you like to explain more?"

34.speaker: Manus Sazon
34.text: "The past two decades have seen a marked increase in workplace accidents, particularly in the sectors of mining and manufacturing."

35.speaker: Manus Sazon
35.text: "Now a cross-industry coalition of employees has bravely approached the Rizian People's Party with a list of requests to convey to our fellow delegates as well as His Majesty."

36.speaker: Manus Sazon
36.text: "Among these are standardized workplace safety protocols, upgraded protective equipment, benefits for those injured on the job, and regular site inspections by state authorities."

37.speaker: Manus Sazon
37.text: "Madam Speaker, Your Majesty, surely you agree on the urgency of this proposition. Rizia's great industries will not flourish as long as our workers are suffering."

39.speaker: Player_Romus
39.text: "It is an honor to be here, Madam Speaker."

41.speaker: Player_Romus
41.text: "I am here to serve you, esteemed delegates. I look forward to your recommendations."

43.speaker: Narrator
43.text: The hall reverberated with full-throated cries of "LONG MAY HE REIGN!" Daria smiled and continued.

45.speaker: Daria de Rava
45.text: "The Delegates will vote on whether to accept or reject it, but this is a non-binding recommendation. The ultimate authority rests with the King and the Royal Council."

46.speaker: Player_Romus
46.text: "So Rusty was right. The RPP took up the workers' cause."

47.speaker: Player_Romus
47.text: "How does he expect us to pay for all this?"

48.speaker: Player_Romus
48.text: "It's hard to believe we had none of these measures in place before now."

49.speaker: Hugo Toras
49.text: "Mr. Montoro will be expecting you to make good on your assurance to him. But of course, you're under no obligation to do so."

50.speaker: Hugo Toras
50.text: "This is why I never brought these meetings to your attention before. The proposals are impractical at best and ruinous at worst."

52.speaker: Narrator
52.text: I suddenly realized the hall had gone quiet.

54.speaker: Player_Romus
54.text: "Please go on. I didn't mean to interrupt."

55.speaker: Player_Romus
55.text: "I've heard enough from the RPP. I'd like to know what Ms. de Rava thinks about the Workers' Protection Act."

57.speaker: Daria de Rava
57.text: "Of course my party believes that worker safety is paramount. But the regulations that have been suggested today amount to overkill."

58.speaker: Daria de Rava
58.text: "Furthermore, they already see employee safety as their responsibility. Shifting that responsibility to the government will do nothing to protect those at risk."

59.speaker: Daria de Rava
59.text: "It will, however, stifle our economic growth and decrease our viability in the global arena."

60.speaker: Daria de Rava
60.text: "My point stands. With tensions rising in both our north and south, we simply cannot afford an extravagance of the type Mr. Sazon is proposing."

61.speaker: Narrator
61.text: From near the front door came the sound of a single person applauding.

62.speaker: Daria de Rava
62.text: "My point stands. Rizia's gold and gas income is far from guaranteed at this moment."
62.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_Military_BlockDrillship"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Pales_ANDORArbitration"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Cede"] == true)

64.speaker: Hugo Toras
64.text: "The delegates will be on their best behavior with you here today."

65.speaker: Narrator
65.text: She had a brisk gait and impeccable posture. The other delegates practically held their breath as they waited for her to take her place.

66.speaker: Hugo Toras
66.text: "In all of the sessions I've attended, she has never made a decision that didn't align with the interests of the noble houses."

67.speaker: Hugo Toras
67.text: "It's now her third term as speaker. I do not believe she intends to vacate the position."

69.speaker: Daria de Rava
69.text: "Today's session is regarding the Rizian Workers' Protection Act."

73.speaker: Hugo Toras
73.text: "You're under no obligation to Mr. Montoro. But I would consider the costs of this proposal before saying yes to it."

74.speaker: Player_Romus
74.text: "Mr. Sazon, I would like to know how Rizia is to pay for these policies."

79.speaker: Manus Sazon
79.text: "The Aureus gas field is expected to generate considerable revenue once Rizian drilling operations begin. I see no harm in running a slight deficit until then."

83.speaker: Manus Sazon
83.text: "After all, in the end, this is a small price to pay for improving thousands of lives."

84.speaker: Manus Sazon
84.text: "Assuming the upcoming arbitrations go our way, the Aureus gas field is expected to generate considerable revenue for Rizia."
84.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Resources_Budget"] > 1) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Buy"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Pales_ANDORArbitration"] == true)

88.speaker: Manus Sazon
88.text: "And in the end, this is a small price to pay for improving thousands of lives."

90.speaker: Manus Sazon
90.text: "As a wise man once said, 'A society is only truly prosperous if every one of its members is able to share in its wealth.'"

94.speaker: Manus Sazon
94.text: "As I was saying, my party and I believe that healthier workers will lead to a more prosperous society."

95.speaker: Manus Sazon
95.text: "What we invest in these measures now will pay off tenfold in the long run."

96.speaker: Manus Sazon
96.text: "What we invest in these measures now will pay off tenfold in the long run."

97.speaker: Narrator
97.text: Manus stepped back from his podium, trying to conceal his disappointment. Daria eagerly approached hers.

101.speaker: Daria de Rava
101.text: "Our focus should be on achieving better diplomatic outcomes with our neighbors, not meddling in the affairs of our corporations."

102.speaker: Manus Sazon
102.text: "Madam Speaker, you are on the board of a construction company yourself. Would you ever advise that it voluntarily undertake the measures we're describing?"

107.speaker: Daria de Rava
107.text: "Our focus should be on bolstering our businesses, not meddling in the affairs of our corporations."

108.speaker: Daria de Rava
108.text: "My point stands. We should not be spending our wealth from the Aureus gas field acquisition before we have even earned it."
108.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_Military_BlockDrillship"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Pales_ANDORArbitration"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Cede"] == true) == false)

109.speaker: Narrator
109.text: Daria sharply knocked on her podium. All eyes turned to her.

110.speaker: Daria de Rava
110.text: "Forgive me, Your Majesty, but I cannot let my opponent continue with these lies."

111.speaker: Narrator
111.text: Manus reluctantly took a step back.

112.speaker: Manus Sazon
112.text: "Our country still has a budget surplus, Your Majesty. One that will only increase once drilling on the Aureus gas field begins."

116.speaker: Manus Sazon
116.text: "Our country still has a budget surplus, Your Majesty."

117.speaker: Manus Sazon
117.text: "What is that wealth for, if not to improve the lives of our citizens?"
117.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Resources_Budget"] > 1) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Buy"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Pales_ANDORArbitration"] == true) == false)

118.speaker: Manus Sazon
118.text: "Besides, a healthy worker is a productive worker. This small investment will pay off tenfold in the long term. For us and for our economy."

119.speaker: Narrator
119.text: I looked towards the source. Rusty was standing in the back of the gallery, dressed in his usual plaid. He nodded at me as he kept clapping.

122.speaker: Player_Romus
122.text: "You didn't tell me that a special guest would be joining us."

126.speaker: Hugo Toras
126.text: "I was not informed. In fact, I'm not certain how Mr. Montoro knew this discussion would be taking place today."

128.speaker: Hugo Toras
128.text: "Unfortunately, these sessions are open to the public."

129.speaker: Hugo Toras
129.text: "We cannot ask him to leave without reason."

130.speaker: Hugo Toras
130.text: "I should have known he'd make an appearance."

131.speaker: Hugo Toras
131.text: "But I presume he is on the side of the RNC. The most he'll do is further expound on the impracticalities of Mr. Sazon's proposal."

132.speaker: Narrator
132.text: Rusty had stopped clapping now. He was scrutinizing me closely, a gleam in his eye.

133.speaker: Daria de Rava
133.text: "How nice of you to join us, Mr. Montoro. Do you have any words on the topic at hand?"

134.speaker: Russello Montoro
134.text: "Call me Rusty, Madam Speaker. And as a matter of fact, I do."

135.speaker: Russello Montoro
135.text: "Now, I won't take up too much of your time. The Baroness of Qaleo summed things up pretty well."

136.speaker: Russello Montoro
136.text: "But I wanted to offer my point of view as a humble business owner of common birth."

137.speaker: Narrator
137.text: Rusty ambled down the aisle of the chamber. He came to a stop between the two speaker podiums.

138.speaker: Player_Romus
138.text: "I side with the delegate majority. The workplace safety proposal from the Rizian People's Party shall not be undertaken."

139.speaker: Player_Romus
139.text: "I overrule the recommendation. The safety measures suggested by the RPP will be implemented in all industries with no exceptions." [-3 Budget, -3 Budget Per Turn]

140.speaker: Player_Romus
140.text: "After listening to compelling arguments from both Mr. Sazon and Mr. Montoro, I hereby order the implementation of the RPP's proposal, with the addendum that the mining industry will be exempt from the new regulations." [-2 Budget To Implement, -1 Budget Per Turn]

142.speaker: Hugo Toras
142.text: "Silence, Mr. Montoro. Do not make His Majesty regret his decision."

143.speaker: Manus Sazon
143.text: "The experts I've consulted with have pinpointed several factors responsible for the rise, chief among them a shortage of skilled labor and growing pressure from our trading partners."

144.speaker: Manus Sazon
144.text: "Simply put, our corporations have been cutting corners, at the expense of human health and safety."

145.speaker: Manus Sazon
145.text: "His Majesty's decree to grant full working permissions to guest workers has helped with the labor shortage, but these employees have been promoted in a rush, making conditions yet more hazardous."

149.speaker: Manus Sazon
149.text: "And of course, financial penalties for corporations that fail to meet these requirements."

150.speaker: Daria de Rava
150.text: "If our businesses are to remain competitive, it is wiser to incentivize good safety practices than to punish their absence."

151.speaker: Narrator
151.text: My uncle gave Rusty a withering look.

156.speaker: Narrator
156.text: My uncle gave Rusty a withering look. Manus stepped back from the podium, his expression hard to read.

157.speaker: Hugo Toras
157.text: "His Majesty has made his decision. Do not question it."

158.speaker: Narrator
158.text: Rusty glared at me, but said nothing.

162.speaker: Hugo Toras
162.text: "Silence, Mr. Montoro. Do not make His Majesty regret his decision."

163.speaker: Narrator
163.text: My uncle gave Rusty a withering look. Manus stepped back from the podium, his face hard to read.

166.speaker: Hugo Toras
166.text: "The Sazon boy will try to pass his latest impractical proposition, and the delegates will sensibly shoot it down."

167.speaker: Hugo Toras
167.text: "The silence from Wehlen has me rather on edge."

168.speaker: Hugo Toras
168.text: "The Pales naval standoff has me rather on edge."

172.speaker: Player_Romus
172.text: "Good that I'm here. It's about time someone listened to that kid."

175.speaker: Hugo Toras
175.text: "There's a reason the King doesn't traditionally attend these sessions."

176.speaker: Player_Romus
176.text: "Impractical? I'll be the judge of that."

177.speaker: Hugo Toras
177.text: "I assure you that you'll agree with me once the arguments are presented."

178.speaker: Hugo Toras
178.text: "The Sazon boy might even keep his speeches to under a half hour."

179.speaker: Player_Romus
179.text: "Joke all you want, but it's about time someone listened to that kid."

180.speaker: Player_Romus
180.text: "Based on what I saw in Sallabes, I doubt it."

181.speaker: Player_Romus
181.text: "You're not jealous of the attention he gets, are you?"

183.speaker: Hugo Toras
183.text: "Ha. Far from it. Although I am worried about the attention he's been getting from one Vina Toras."

184.speaker: Hugo Toras
184.text: "His speech there seemed to have done a number on your daughter."

185.speaker: Player_Romus
185.text: "It's not a standoff. Just insurance in case things go south at the AN."

186.speaker: Player_Romus
186.text: "Trust me, I'll be glad when it's over."

191.speaker: Hugo Toras
191.text: "I trust Duchess Azaro is capable of de-escalation if necessary."

195.speaker: Player_Romus
195.text: "Me, too. I hope your son's gambit worked."

196.speaker: Player_Romus
196.text: "President Smolak will be at the next AN session. We can corner him there if we need to."

197.speaker: Player_Romus
197.text: "Nothing we can do about it now. Let's focus on today's meeting."

198.speaker: Player_Romus
198.text: "I hope the investigators haven't found anything damning."

199.speaker: Hugo Toras
199.text: "Madam Speaker, let the record show that the King has aligned with the House majority."

200.speaker: Hugo Toras
200.text: "Madam Speaker, let the record show that the King has overridden the House majority."

202.speaker: Narrator
202.text: Daria made a note in her binder, then looked up at Hugo and myself. If she was bothered by my decision, her face didn't show it.

203.speaker: Daria de Rava
203.text: "Once again, I thank His Majesty for blessing us with his presence today."

204.speaker: Daria de Rava
204.text: "And Grand Vizier Hugo Toras for presiding over the session."

206.speaker: Narrator
206.text: Daria made a note in her binder, then looked up at me, slightly smiling.

208.speaker: Daria de Rava
208.text: "My fellow delegates and esteemed guests, this meeting is now adjourned. Any follow-up questions will be addressed in future sittings."

209.speaker: Narrator
209.text: She rang the bell again, and the room began to empty out.

210.speaker: Narrator
210.text: As the guards escorted me and Hugo towards the exit, I noticed Rusty still standing in the hall with his arms folded.

214.speaker: Player_Romus
214.text: "Sorry, Rusty. I couldn't make it look like I was playing favorites."

216.speaker: Player_Romus
216.text: "Well? I'm a man of my word, aren't I?"

217.speaker: Player_Romus
217.text: "Don't make me regret listening to you."

218.speaker: Russello Montoro
218.text: "And I'm a man of mine, Your Majesty."

219.speaker: Player_Romus
219.text: "You never seriously thought I was going to give in to you, did you?"

220.speaker: Russello Montoro
220.text: "You're the king. It's your prerogative to change your mind."

221.speaker: Russello Montoro
221.text: "Sure, Your Majesty. I hear you loud and clear."

222.speaker: Russello Montoro
222.text: "None, Your Majesty. We're all just playing games here."

223.speaker: Player_Romus
223.text: "No need to thank me. You and I wanted this equally."

224.speaker: Narrator
224.text: He bowed to each of us in turn before hurrying back into the building.

230.speaker: Narrator
230.text: He looked at me and winked.

231.speaker: Russello Montoro
231.text: "Now. The Rizian Standard Dictionary defines 'gold' as a yellow precious metal, used in jewelry and to guarantee the value of currencies."

232.speaker: Player_Romus
232.text: "There will be no bloviating in these chambers, *Rusty*."

233.speaker: Player_Romus
233.text: "Yes, we are all familiar with the substance in question."

235.speaker: Russello Montoro
235.text: "But in Rizia, it's so much more. Commoners who've never even touched a ducat still feel proud to live 'on shores of gold', as we sing."

236.speaker: Russello Montoro
236.text: "Fair enough, Your Majesty. Mr. Sazon over there has done enough bloviating for all of us put together."

237.speaker: Russello Montoro
237.text: "But our shores would never have been golden in the first place if our monarchs had listened to naysayers like Mr. Sazon here."

238.speaker: Russello Montoro
238.text: "Your Majesty, your predecessors knew that there can be no prosperity without hard work. Our grit and determination today fills the nation's coffers tomorrow."

239.speaker: Russello Montoro
239.text: "But where does that grit go when the government's got our hands tied? How can we function as a company when you folks don't trust us to take care of our own people?"

240.speaker: Manus Sazon
240.text: "If I may ask, sir, how exactly would our proposal tie your hands? What is so difficult about regulating safety in gold mines?"

241.speaker: Russello Montoro
241.text: "Don't play dumb, kid. You know each mining site in Rizia is as unique as a birthmark on the Archpriest of Deyr's behind."

242.speaker: Manus Sazon
242.text: "They would be paid for in equal measure by the government and the corporations in question."

243.speaker: Daria de Rava
243.text: "Mr. Montoro, I assume you are here as a representative of RRG as well as Rizia's business community as a whole. Is it safe to say your fellow executives share your opinion on the RPP's proposal?"

245.speaker: Russello Montoro
245.text: "Oh, it's very safe to say that. Although it does strike me that your opponent's proposal could be implemented in, say, the construction industry without too much difficulty."

246.speaker: Narrator
246.text: Daria's grip on her podium tightened. Rusty stroked his chin faux-thoughtfully.

247.speaker: Russello Montoro
247.text: "Come to think of it, I won't presume to speak up for the people in Madam Speaker's high-and-mighty 'circles'. I'm the only one who cared enough to show up today, right?"

248.speaker: Russello Montoro
248.text: "So here's another thought. You regulate Rizian industry however you want. But maybe, just maybe, you think about making an exception for old Rusty."

249.speaker: Narrator
249.text: He winked at me again. Manus drew a hand across his brow.

250.speaker: Manus Sazon
250.text: "Our proposal as it stands does not allow for exceptions. The King may alter it as he sees fit, but the RPP refuses to do so."

251.speaker: Player_Romus
251.text: "Giving *some* of the workers what they want might divide them enough to head off organized dissent, right?"

255.speaker: Narrator
255.text: Manus drew a hand across his brow.

256.speaker: Russello Montoro
256.text: "But I'll just say this. There's no way we at RRG can keep filling your government's coffers if our hands are tied by unnecessary regulations."

257.speaker: Player_Romus
257.text: "Your proposal was never going to be accepted in its entirety, Mr. Sazon. Compromise is part of the political process."

258.speaker: Player_Romus
258.text: "I've witnessed Mr. Montoro's cavalier attitude towards employee safety. If any company needs to be regulated, it's RRG."

259.speaker: Player_Romus
259.text: "I don't agree with Mr. Montoro's arguments one bit. It doesn't make sense to regulate some industries and not others."

261.speaker: Daria de Rava
261.text: "What it will do is hamper the majority of Rizian businesses while giving miners an unfair advantage."

262.speaker: Manus Sazon
262.text: "My party will not compromise when human welfare is at stake."

265.speaker: Russello Montoro
265.text: "Cavalier? Heck, Your Majesty, you're the one who'd be putting men out of work with one decree."

267.speaker: Hugo Toras
267.text: "The time for a vote is drawing close. To be clear, Mr. Sazon, you do not wish to amend your proposal to take into account Mr. Montoro's comments?"

268.speaker: Daria de Rava
268.text: "Please do not forget in whose presence you're speaking, Mr. Montoro."

269.speaker: Manus Sazon
269.text: "I do not, Your Grace. The King may choose to accept or ignore them at will."

270.speaker: Player_Romus
270.text: "Rusty, did you have any closing arguments?"

271.speaker: Player_Romus
271.text: "I'd like to confer with my Grand Vizier."

273.speaker: Manus Sazon
273.text: "I've stated my case, Your Majesty. But I will say this."

274.speaker: Manus Sazon
274.text: "This proposal would fail without you in this room. So I'd like to believe you've joined us for a reason."

278.speaker: Manus Sazon
278.text: "I'm glad you joined us in this room today. Perhaps now you have a better sense of how His Majesty Valero's system was designed to function."

279.speaker: Manus Sazon
279.text: "The majority of delegates in this room support noble interests. Not those of the subjects they claim to represent."

280.speaker: Manus Sazon
280.text: "As long as that is true, it is the King's responsibility to see past the lies and make the decision that best serves ordinary citizens."

283.speaker: Narrator
283.text: We turned away from the Delegates and spoke in low voices.

284.speaker: Player_Romus
284.text: "I told Manus I wanted to work closer with him. Would I be throwing away that chance if I shot down his proposal?"

288.speaker: Player_Romus
288.text: "I can't ignore the potential benefits of cooperating with RRG. Can I?"

291.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
291.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Manus_WorkWithRPP"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Manus_ConstitutionalMonarchy"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Manus_OverthrowMonarchy"] == true) == false

292.speaker: Daria de Rava
292.text: "All those in favor of the RPP's worker safety proposal, raise your hands."

293.speaker: Narrator
293.text: About a quarter of the delegates, mostly those with green sashes, put a hand in the air.

294.speaker: Daria de Rava
294.text: "Those in favor of encouraging Rizian businesses -- *all* businesses -- to develop and enforce their own safety protocols on a voluntary basis?"

295.speaker: Narrator
295.text: The rest of the delegates -- an overwhelming majority -- raised their hands.

296.speaker: Daria de Rava
296.text: "The Delegates have an official recommendation. Rather than introduce sweeping and expensive labor reforms, Rizia should entrust the matter of safety to its business owners."

299.speaker: Daria de Rava
299.text: "The final decision is now in the hands of His Majesty King Romus."

300.speaker: Daria de Rava
300.text: "Will you accept or overrule the Delegates' recommendation?"

301.speaker: Player_Romus
301.text: "Would I lose face with the Delegates if I implemented a proposal they voted against?"

302.speaker: Player_Romus
302.text: "What do you think about Rusty's exception idea? Could I decide to exempt RRG from the new regulations?"

303.speaker: Hugo Toras
303.text: "Then you have the floor, Madam Speaker."

304.speaker: Daria de Rava
304.text: "Thank you, Your Grace. As a reminder to you and His Majesty, this vote serves to demonstrate the opinion of the Rizian populace, and is a non-binding recommendation."

305.speaker: Hugo Toras
305.text: "It would be highly unusual, Your Majesty."

307.speaker: Hugo Toras
307.text: "Why would you-- Well. I'm sure you had a good reason."

308.speaker: Hugo Toras
308.text: "Valero never rejected a recommendation in all his years as king."

309.speaker: Hugo Toras
309.text: "You're the king. Of course you can."

310.speaker: Hugo Toras
310.text: "The young man does seem desperate to have you in his corner. I suspect the princess has something to do with that."

314.speaker: Player_Romus
314.text: "Would I be making an enemy of Manus Sazon's party and his house if I shot down his proposal?"
314.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Manus_WorkWithRPP"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Manus_ConstitutionalMonarchy"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Manus_OverthrowMonarchy"] == true) == false

316.speaker: Hugo Toras
316.text: "His party is the enemy already. Granting them your favor will strengthen their chances in the next election, and commensurately weaken the monarchy."

317.speaker: Hugo Toras
317.text: "It would save the kingdom money, it would send Mr. Montoro over the moon and it would partly placate the complainers in the RPP."

318.speaker: Hugo Toras
318.text: "However, it would have a significant effect on Rizia's other corporations, many of which are owned by nobles such as Baroness de Rava and her constituents."

319.speaker: Hugo Toras
319.text: "In this case, accepting the RPP's proposal would be deleterious to the economies of the provinces the Delegates represent."

320.speaker: Hugo Toras
320.text: "Mr. Montoro did imply that staying on good terms with his company would earn you the right to buy back the former royal stake."

321.speaker: Hugo Toras
321.text: "If we want to continue as a resource-based economy, owning more of RG would be advisable."

324.speaker: Player_Romus
324.text: "Have you said all that you wanted to say, Mr. Sazon?"

326.speaker: Narrator
326.text: Everyone in the room went silent as they awaited my next words.

330.speaker: Russello Montoro
330.text: "It seems to me like the decision you have to make is no decision at all."

331.speaker: Russello Montoro
331.text: "You could even walk out of this room right now and let your legislative system do the rest."

332.speaker: Russello Montoro
332.text: "But you're a man of action. I know you want the final say. So by all means, go on and say it."

335.speaker: Narrator
335.text: He reached out to shake my hand. I suddenly felt the cool of metal against my palm.

336.speaker: Russello Montoro
336.text: "My guys dug this up in the MITZ a while back. Consider it a token of my appreciation."

339.speaker: Player_Romus
339.text: "You've gotten what you wanted. No need for bribery."

341.speaker: Russello Montoro
341.text: "Heck if I know. Looks pretty old, though, doesn't it?"

342.speaker: Russello Montoro
342.text: "Who do you think I am? This is out of the goodness of my heart."

343.speaker: Russello Montoro
343.text: "As for those revisions to the RRG shareholder contract... my lawyers will be in touch with the paperwork."

365.speaker: Manus Sazon
365.text: "Now a cross-industry coalition of employees and guest workers has bravely approached the Rizian People's Party with a list of requests to convey to our fellow delegates as well as His Majesty."

366.speaker: Manus Sazon
366.text: "Our industries' continued reliance on guest workers, who are paid and trained less than their native Rizian counterparts, is exacerbating the problem."

382.speaker: Player_Romus
382.text: "Is there something you'd like to say to me?"

385.speaker: Russello Montoro
385.text: "One moment of your time, Your Majesty."

386.speaker: Player_Romus
386.text: "You've been hoarding this? It belongs to the Crown."

387.speaker: Russello Montoro
387.text: "Finders keepers, I always thought. But hey, it's yours now."

389.speaker: Narrator
389.text: He eyed me coolly as Hugo and I passed him and walked out.

390.speaker: Narrator
390.text: He extended his hand for a handshake.

393.speaker: Narrator
393.text: I withdrew my hand and took a closer look at the object he'd given me.

394.speaker: Russello Montoro
394.text: "Your act of benevolence will not be forgotten, Your Majesty."

395.speaker: Russello Montoro
395.text: "I just wanted to express my gratitude, Your Majesty."

399.speaker: Russello Montoro
399.text: "See you real soon, Your Majesty. Your Grace."

400.speaker: Russello Montoro
400.text: "If you'll recall, I also mentioned the possibility of revising the RRG shareholder contract. You interested?"

401.speaker: Player_Romus
401.text: "Thank you, but no. The Kingdom's share in RRG will stay the same."

402.speaker: Player_Romus
402.text: "Perhaps. I'd have to know more details first."

403.speaker: Player_Romus
403.text: "I've given some thought to it and, yes, I would like to alter Rizia's share."

404.speaker: Russello Montoro
404.text: "Your wish is my command. I'll have my lawyers get in touch with the paperwork."

409.speaker: Player_Romus
409.text: "For what it's worth, you made a good case."

411.speaker: Russello Montoro
411.text: "We'll get to work on those regulations straight away. But I wasn't kidding about our gold output suffering."

412.speaker: Russello Montoro
412.text: "Much obliged, Your Majesty. No hard feelings."

419.speaker: Player_Romus
419.text: "While I sympathize with the RPP, our treasury is too strained for this proposal. It will not be implemented at this time."

424.speaker: Hugo Toras
424.text: "He seemed to have caught your attention in Sallabes."

425.speaker: Hugo Toras
425.text: "Rebuilding relations with House Sazon is a sound strategy. But we mustn't allow them to get too close to the throne."

426.speaker: Hugo Toras
426.text: "Rebuilding relations with House Sazon is a sound strategy. As long as you don't buy into their nonsense."

433.speaker: Hugo Toras
433.text: "They're a fool for rhetoric over in Brenas. We mustn't allow ourselves to be so easily suckered in."

434.speaker: Hugo Toras
434.text: "When you have enough power, attention is nothing but a hindrance."

435.speaker: Russello Montoro
435.text: "Raising the stake won't be free, naturally. But I'll give you a royal discount."

436.speaker: Daria de Rava
436.text: "The RNC is not willing to compromise, either."

440.speaker: Hugo Toras
440.text: "However, if the goal is to diversify our economy away from resources, that 15 percent barely matters."

441.speaker: Daria de Rava
441.text: "Rizia's other major corporations -- run by families with much longer and illustrious histories than that of Mr. Montoro here -- should not be punished simply because they do not happen to produce gold."

442.speaker: Narrator
442.text: I heard whispers of agreement from several other RNC members.

443.speaker: Manus Sazon
443.text: "That you would refer to these perfectly reasonable suggestions as a 'punishment' is indicative of where your loyalties lie, Madam Speaker."

444.speaker: Russello Montoro
444.text: "I've got to head out and spread the bad news. See you real soon, Your Majesty. Your Grace."

448.speaker: Russello Montoro
448.text: "It might be time to think about finding new gold sources. Just to keep us in the black."
448.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Economy_QalusGoldMine_Completed"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Economy_QalusGoldMine_Project"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Enable_Policy_RD_Economy_QalusGoldMineProject"] == true) == false)

452.speaker: Russello Montoro
452.text: "At least the new mine in Qalus will keep us in the black. Just about."

453.speaker: Russello Montoro
453.text: "You might want to think about digging under your relations' estates in Valenqiris after all. Just to keep us in the black."
453.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Economy_QalusGoldMine_Completed"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_RD_Economy_QalusGoldMine_Project"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Enable_Policy_RD_Economy_QalusGoldMineProject"] == true)

457.speaker: Narrator
457.text: He bowed to me, then jauntily straightened up and walked out the door.

465.speaker: Manus Sazon
465.text: "Your Majesty. Thank you so much for attending today's session. And for implementing our proposal, of course."

469.speaker: Manus Sazon
469.text: "Your Majesty. Thank you so much for attending today's session. Implementing even part of our proposal was more than we could have hoped for."

470.speaker: Manus Sazon
470.text: "Your Majesty. I cannot thank you enough for attending today's session."

471.speaker: Narrator
471.text: Manus' eyes traveled involuntarily to the street, where one of Rusty's guards was helping the gold magnate into a shiny black Kadilla.

473.speaker: Narrator
473.text: Behind him, leaning against the wall, were two of the Arcasian guards I'd seen in Bronaz.

474.speaker: Player_Romus
474.text: "Is this going to be a problem?"

476.speaker: Hugo Toras
476.text: "I can't say I'm happy to see Mr. Montoro in these halls."

477.speaker: Narrator
477.text: He gave Manus a brusque nod. The opposition speaker didn't acknowledge it.

478.speaker: Narrator
478.text: Scandalized chatter broke out among the Delegates. Daria banged her gavel for silence.

479.speaker: Russello Montoro
479.text: "Point is, there's no one-size-fits-all protocol for regulating what we do. The environment, the ore density, the tech being used -- it all varies, even within parts of the same mine."

480.speaker: Russello Montoro
480.text: "We're doing our best to keep our workers safe on the job. But we also want them to go home with healthy paychecks."

482.speaker: Player_Romus
482.text: "What about the miners who have been speaking out? We cannot ignore their complaints."

483.speaker: Russello Montoro
483.text: "Your Majesty, esteemed Delegates -- if we're forced to develop specialized protocols for every single nook and cranny of our business, we'll end up millions in the hole. Who even knows if anyone will be safer for it."

484.speaker: Player_Romus
484.text: "You could easily afford such measures if you forewent a portion of your own salary."

486.speaker: Russello Montoro
486.text: "I beg your pardon, but half the people in this room are sitting on fortunes just because they happen to have the right last name. Asking a hard-working commoner to give up the money he spent his life scraping for -- it doesn't sit right with me."

487.speaker: Russello Montoro
487.text: "RRG takes care of our own, Your Majesty. We'll solve this within our company, like we always have."

488.speaker: Russello Montoro
488.text: "Hey, if you want to test my theory, you're more than welcome to do so."

489.speaker: Player_Romus
489.text: "That does seem much more complicated than Mr. Sazon made it out to be."

490.speaker: Russello Montoro
490.text: "Yes, well, he's a noble. Sooner or later, he's got to butt heads with the way the world really works."

491.speaker: Narrator
491.text: A quiet look of annoyance flashed across Daria's face.

493.speaker: Daria de Rava
493.text: "The subject of noble wealth is hardly germane to this discussion."

494.speaker: Hugo Toras
494.text: "And if we are to increase our stake, it would behoove us not to damage RRG's profitability."

495.speaker: Hugo Toras
495.text: "Passing a version that exempts RRG makes practical sense, but would surely anger the nobles whose investments are affected."

496.speaker: Hugo Toras
496.text: "As for his family, I don't believe House Sazon had a hand in this proposal at all. They have as much to lose from it as the Azaros or Torases."

497.speaker: Hugo Toras
497.text: "But I urge you to make the decision that benefits Rizia, not Mr. Sazon or his party."

498.speaker: Hugo Toras
498.text: "The young man does seem desperate to have you in his corner."

504.speaker: Narrator
504.text: He bowed, then began whistling jauntily as he walked past me and out the door.

505.speaker: Narrator
505.text: Hugo shook his head with disdain.

506.speaker: Hugo Toras
506.text: "You were right not to grant him an exception. That man's ego does not need any further inflation."

510.speaker: Hugo Toras
510.text: "Exempting RRG from the new regulations was a logical compromise, but I do hope it won't inflate that man's ego any further."

514.speaker: Hugo Toras
514.text: "You were right to side with the RNC. The more of Rizian Royal Gold we can snatch back from that man's hands, the better."

515.speaker: Hugo Toras
515.text: "I'm still curious how he found out that today's session was taking place. It would be most unlike Speaker de Rava to inform him."

516.speaker: Narrator
516.text: As we stepped outside the House of Delegates, I saw Manus Sazon waiting to greet us.

517.speaker: Player_Romus
517.text: "I'm happy to have gotten a look into the inner workings of the House of Delegates. It was very enlightening indeed."

518.speaker: Player_Romus
518.text: "My foremost concern is for the Rizian economy. I hope you understand."

519.speaker: Player_Romus
519.text: "You're most welcome. We shall have to meet soon to discuss the next steps."

520.speaker: Player_Romus
520.text: "I hope you aren't too disappointed with the outcome."

521.speaker: Manus Sazon
521.text: "I hope that means you'll continue to consider our proposals going forward."

522.speaker: Manus Sazon
522.text: "You're welcome to attend as often as you'd like."

524.speaker: Manus Sazon
524.text: "Not at all. I see the merit in my opponents' arguments, and I understand your decision completely."

525.speaker: Manus Sazon
525.text: "I understand completely. I'll make sure our future proposals are more economically feasible."

526.speaker: Narrator
526.text: Hugo gave him a thin-lipped smile.

530.speaker: Hugo Toras
530.text: "Congratulations, Mr. Sazon. I'm sure you and your party will be celebrating today's triumph."

531.speaker: Manus Sazon
531.text: "Indeed, Your Grace. His Majesty's ruling was... much more than I ever could have hoped for."

535.speaker: Hugo Toras
535.text: "Congratulations, Mr. Sazon. I hope your party isn't terribly disappointed about the exemption for Mr. Montoro's corporation."

536.speaker: Narrator
536.text: Manus' eyes traveled involuntarily to the street, where one of Rusty's guards was helping the gold magnate into a shiny black Kadilla.

537.speaker: Narrator
537.text: A look seemed to pass between the two of them. What it meant, I wasn't certain.

538.speaker: Manus Sazon
538.text: "Of course many of my colleagues wanted more... But in my opinion, His Majesty's ruling is still cause for celebration."

539.speaker: Hugo Toras
539.text: "You did well today, Mr. Sazon. I hope you and your party aren't too disappointed."

540.speaker: Narrator
540.text: Manus' eyes traveled involuntarily to the street, where one of Rusty's guards was helping the gold magnate into a shiny black Kadilla.

541.speaker: Narrator
541.text: A look seemed to pass between the two of them. What it meant, I wasn't certain.

542.speaker: Narrator
542.text: A look seemed to pass between the two of them. What it meant, I wasn't certain.

543.speaker: Manus Sazon
543.text: "A temporary setback, Your Grace. We'll continue to push for the well-being of all Rizians, to the extent that our limited forum allows."

544.speaker: Manus Sazon
544.text: "I won't trouble either of you any longer. Thanks once more and good afternoon."

546.speaker: Player_Romus
546.text: "Ah. Just the man I wanted to see."

548.speaker: Daria de Rava
548.text: "The business owners in my circles, most of whose companies span generations, cannot simply transform their practices at the whim of the government."

549.speaker: Daria de Rava
549.text: "The views of the nobility are hardly germane to this discussion."
